title: Design System: CAI Verify Security Console

display.purpose: One screen title, never a marketing hero.

title.purpose: Row groups, dialogs, and direction labels.

label.purpose: Controls, field names, and status labels.

mono.purpose: Bounded identifiers, timestamps, paths, and technical values.

shadows.name: temporary-popover
shadows.purpose: Separates a temporary popover from the current task.

shadows.name: modal-overlay
shadows.purpose: Separates a modal from its dimmed background without a decorative border.

motion.name: state-feedback
motion.purpose: Hover, focus, active, selection, and status feedback.

motion.name: panel-transition
motion.purpose: Small workflow and disclosure panel transitions.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Removes translation and completes nonessential transitions immediately.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Starts the one primary action in a decision area.

components.name: Secondary Button

narrative.overview:
The console is designed for a security engineer reviewing bounded evidence at a technical workstation, often for an extended period and sometimes under incident-response pressure. It should feel calm, exact, and durable in mixed office light. Density is disciplined rather than sparse: important relationships stay visible, while decoration stays out of the operator's path.

The workflow is linear and honest. Configuration leads to readiness, readiness to explicit confirmation, execution to two-direction results, and results to verified evidence. Responsive layouts preserve that order from 320 pixels through large desktops. The system follows the user's light or dark preference by default and allows an in-memory theme change without saving browser state.

This system explicitly rejects AWS-console sprawl, generic card-grid dashboards, generic AI-tool chrome, compliance-certificate theater, and consumer onboarding that hides technical boundaries.
keyCharacteristics: Familiar controls with no invented interaction vocabulary.
Restrained color, with status carried by text and icons as well as hue.
Responsive state transitions with no decorative choreography.
Explicit limitations and integrity state adjacent to every result.

rules.name: The Ten Percent Rule
rules.body: Forensic Teal occupies no more than 10 percent of a screen. Its scarcity identifies action and state.

rules.name: The Status Pairing Rule
rules.body: Every status combines an icon and explicit text. Color is never the only carrier of meaning.

rules.name: The Evidence Is Readable Rule
rules.body: Never reduce a technical value below 0.8125rem or use color contrast as a substitute for typographic hierarchy.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Buttons, labels, navigation, and status text use sentence case. All-caps copy is forbidden.

rules.name: The Flat By Default Rule
rules.body: Work surfaces remain flat at rest. Shadows exist only to explain a temporary layer above the current task.

rules.name: The One Boundary Rule
rules.body: A component may use a divider, tonal contrast, or a shadow to establish its boundary, never all three.

dos: Do keep configuration, readiness, execution, results, and evidence in one visible workflow order.
Do use Forensic Teal only for primary action, current selection, links, and positive state.
Do pair every status color with a distinct icon and explicit text.
Do preserve a 44px minimum pointer target where controls are not already part of a compact desktop field group.
Do retain keyboard order, visible focus, semantic landmarks, and meaningful headings from 320 pixels through 200 percent zoom.
Do reveal sensitive configuration only after an explicit action, then conceal it after 30 seconds, navigation, tab loss, or operator request.
donts: Don't recreate AWS-console sprawl with many unrelated services, nested navigation, and competing panels.
Don't use generic card-grid dashboards and hero metrics that obscure the actual workflow.
Don't use generic AI-tool chrome such as purple gradients, neon accents, glassmorphism, and decorative model imagery.
Don't use compliance-certificate theater or copy that implies one passing run establishes compliance.
Don't use consumer onboarding that hides technical boundaries or turns exact authorization into a one-click promise.
Don't add decorative motion, page-load choreography, gradient text, colored side-stripe borders, or wide ghost-card shadows.
Don't expose sensitive values through tooltips, truncated text, copy controls, browser storage, or visual debug output.
